Subject: MedVault - Private hosting discovery & next steps

Emily — thanks again for the time today. Per our call, I wanted to capture the key pains, success criteria, and proposed immediate next steps so your procurement and infra teams have a single reference. TL;DR: MedVault needs a private/VPC deployment with customer-managed keys, strict egress controls (no outbound except through customer proxy), and an option for an air-gapped export workflow.

Summary of pain points you shared:
- PHI/data residency constraints: all patient data must remain in customer-controlled network enclaves; no vendor-hosted copies outside agreed VPC.
- Risk of unauthorized egress: current vendor telemetry and agent-level egress caused a compliance review.
- Key control: legal/infosec require FIPS-compatible keys and the ability to rotate/export/import keys (HSM-backed preferred).
- Latency for real-time assist: <200ms p95 target for short inference (under 1k tokens) in regional DC.

Current stack and constraints you described:
- Core services run on-prem Kubernetes (k8s 1.27) + Oracle DB for records.
- Nginx reverse proxies and an outbound proxy appliance that mediates all egress.
- SOC2 Type II in progress; some environments require monthly change freezes / offline export approvals.

Success criteria (what MedVault would call a "go/no-go"):
- Deployment inside customer VPC or on-prem with no unapproved external egress.
- Customer-managed KMS/HSM integration with key import/rotation and audit logs accessible to MedVault.
- Security questionnaire answered and baseline pen-test/attestation handshake in place.
- A short PoC (2–4 weeks) demonstrating inference against a synthetic PHI-like dataset and meeting latency & cost targets.

Immediate next steps we committed to:
- I will share a first-draft network diagram and a private-deploy overview (attached).
- Karthik will run a technical deep-dive next week on KMS/HSM integration and provide a checklist for the proxy requirements.
- Monica will start a SOW template and a ballpark estimate for reserved capacity (SLA+support).
- Emily: please confirm the right technical contacts for the IT/infrastructure and procurement threads (email addresses below would help).

Attachments: medvault_redwood_arch_diagram_v1.png (PNG, 210KB), redwood_private_deploy_overview.pdf (PDF, 320KB), MedVault_Security_Q_v1.xlsx (XLSX, 52KB)

Thanks again — will follow up with the diagram and proposed times for the technical deep-dive.

From: Emily Shaw <emily.shaw@medvault.com>

Date: Sun, 09 May 2027 17:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MedVault - Private hosting discovery & next steps

Alex — appreciate the clear recap, this is very helpful. A few clarifications from my side after chatting with our infra lead Tom:
- Timeline: procurement is aiming for a decision window in the next 6–8 weeks; ideal PoC start in June.
- Air-gap: for our archival export workflows we need an operational process that allows for an offline transfer; if Redwood can provide an offline bundle export flow (signed artifacts + checksum) that's a big plus.
- HSM: we do require HSM-backed keys for production; we can support either AWS CloudHSM (in our VPC) or an on-prem HSM that supports PKCS#11.
- Egress: outbound to an approved proxy is fine; the proxy enforces strict allow-lists. Any telemetry or usage metrics must be opt-in and routed to an internal endpoint.

I've copied Tom Li <tom.li@medvault.com> (infra) and procurement@medvault.com on follow-ups but for now use me as the primary contact. Please include a high-level procurement checklist in the SOW so our Purchasing team sees next steps early.

Thanks — Emily
Emily Shaw
Head of Product, MedVault Health
